summary: The server needs a pid file
detail: Asked for by Peter, 19 Sep 2026. Purpose to confirm (stopping a stray dev server, or a process manager in production?): it decides the default path and whether a pid file naming a live process (process.kill(pid, 0)) should stop a second server starting. Shape: write process.pid at startup and remove it on exit, SIGINT and SIGTERM; path from an env var in config.ts; the code in its own module, since main.ts is resources and routes only. Care points: bun --hot re-runs main.ts in the same process on every reload, so exit handlers must be registered once per process, not once per reload; bun test loads .env (checked) and server.test.ts spawns its server with the runner's env, so the test server must not overwrite or delete the dev server's pid file; gitignore the file.
note: 19 Sep 2026: purpose never confirmed, so built as both a handle and a lock. server/pid.ts writes ./duckdown.pid before listening (DUCKDOWN_PID moves it, empty turns it off), refuses to start if it names another live process, and removes it on exit, SIGINT and SIGTERM (registered once per process for --hot). *.pid is gitignored; tests give each server its own pid file and cover write, refusal and removal. Proved in use the same day: the desktop app reported the preview server stopped while bun run dev and the server still held :8080; kill $(cat duckdown.pid) stopped it, the file went and the port freed.

summary: The editor's file list is empty: railroad 0.11's keyed list() hands each row a Signal, and Browser.tsx reads it as a plain item
detail: Found 19 Sep 2026 demoing the editor, signed in: /edit/pages/ answers 200 with index.md, -theme.css and guide/, yet the list shows no rows. In 0.11.0's keyed form list(items, keyFn, render), render receives ReadonlySignal<T> (node_modules/@blueshed/railroad/jsx.ts, the list() overloads), so f.name is undefined and f.name.endsWith(...) throws. After its first render list() re-syncs synchronously inside files.set(), so the throw lands in load()'s bare catch {}: no console error, and folders.set() never runs. ImageBrowser.tsx has the same keyed rows (f.name; f.path in the thumbnail src and onclick), so expect rows there with no names and a src of /edit/browseundefined (not yet seen). New in the uncommitted 0.0.2 upgrade from 0.1.1; the server tests can't see it. Fix shape: read the row signal in each keyed render (f$.peek() in handlers, f$.map(...) for text), or use the index-based list(items, (f) => ...) form; and stop the empty catch hiding render errors. While it's broken, hasTheme is never set (it comes after the throwing files.set), so New offers Theme even where a -theme.css exists (seen at the root, 19 Sep 2026); choosing it overwrites that file (todo 8).
note: 19 Sep 2026: Browser.tsx and ImageBrowser.tsx read rows with f$.map(...) and f$.peek(); both load()s moved the signal updates out of the try, so a render error now surfaces (one did, from a half-edited hot reload). Written 20 Mar: it taught plaintext passwords in users.json (hashes since 0.0.2), themes per folder only (they cascade), hard-coded theme colours (variables now), {{title}} defaulting to "duckdown" (it's "duckie"), click-to-copy images (it's select, then Copy Markdown); it knew nothing of toc, callouts, wiki links, heading links, dark mode, the nav marks, New's no-overwrite, or the nav cache; and its name (duckdown-authoring) didn't match its folder.
note: 19 Sep 2026: rewritten as a lean SKILL.md (where the content lives, writing a page, the six traps, how to check) plus reference.md with a contents list (content folder, pages and URLs, front matter, markdown, navigation, themes and every variable, template, static files and images, users, the editor, troubleshooting), following the skill-creator's pattern and railroad's bun-route. name: duckdown; a fuller, more assertive description. Claims checked against the code. CLAUDE.md now says to update the skill and the guide pages whenever a content feature changes.

summary: A folder's URL (/guide/ or /guide) is a 404: only /guide/index.html works
detail: Noted 19 Sep 2026 writing the skill: the site route maps a path to <path>.md, so /guide/ looks for 'guide/.md' and /guide for 'guide.md'. Serve the folder's index.md for both, the way / already serves index.md; the nav could then link folders as /guide/.
note: 2026-09-19: site.ts resolves a folder to its index.md — /blog, /blog/ and /blog/index.html all serve the same page. Wiki links and the nav still emit index.html, so nothing else changed.

summary: A page whose first line reads like 'Update: closed Monday' loses it to the front matter
detail: Found 19 Sep 2026 writing the skill: parseFrontMatter takes any leading 'word: text' lines as metadata, so a page without front matter that opens with such a sentence silently drops it (checked). The skill now warns (start with a heading or a blank line). Options: treat only known keys (title, theme, nav, toc, x-…) as front matter; or require the blank line that ends it; or YAML-style --- fences.
note: 2026-09-19: front matter is now either a --- fence or the known keys (title, theme, nav, toc, layout, description, draft, date, and x-* for your own). 'Update: closed Monday' is a paragraph again. Breaking for anyone who invented their own bare keys — use x- or a fence.

summary: New sites lose the authoring skill: bun create's setup deletes .claude
detail: Noted 19 Sep 2026: setup removes the whole .claude folder, which now holds the duckdown authoring skill (what a Claude session writing the new site's content should read), railroad's skills and launch.json (the preview pane). Decide what a new site keeps: likely skills/duckdown and launch.json; railroad and bun-route only matter to someone changing the editor.

summary: The duck logo kept its own black, in every theme, and vanished in dark mode
detail: Peter asked 19 Sep 2026 whether CSS can colour the duck. It was placed with , and an SVG shown that way is a separate document: the page's CSS and variables can't reach inside it, and currentColor means the file's own colour. On the dark theme the black duck was invisible.
note: 19 Sep 2026: the page now has an empty and the theme paints it: background: var(--duck, currentColor) with the SVG as a -webkit-mask/mask (contain, centred); the eye and wing are holes, so the page still shows through. The duckdown theme sets --duck: var(--accent), so it is teal in light and dark. Two things learned the hard way, both now in the Images guide and the skill: .

summary: Pages written as files don't reach the nav until an editor save or a restart
detail: Seen 19 Sep 2026 adding a blog with the authoring skill: the post rendered at once, but Blog only joined the nav after saving the page in the editor (the cache is dropped by the editor's writes, todo 22). That's fine for the editor, but anyone — or any Claude session — writing pages as files meets it every time. Options: don't cache when DEBUG=1; or check the newest mtime under pages/ (local storage only, an extra stat per request); or leave it, since the skill and CLAUDE.md both say so.
note: 19 Sep 2026: Peter chose the development exception. siteNav(pages, debug = DEBUG) builds per request when DEBUG is on and caches otherwise; navChanged() still drops it in production. Checked on the running dev server: a folder's index.md written straight to disk joined the nav immediately, and left it when deleted, with no editor save. The skill, CLAUDE.md and the CHANGELOG now say so; a unit test covers both ways.

summary: {{pages}} expanded inside code, so no page could show the tag
detail: The listing was substituted across the whole rendered page, including <code> spans and fenced blocks. The guide page documenting {{pages}} had the guide's own folder listing injected into its code sample and its inline code, so the one page that must show the syntax couldn't. Found while checking the seed site for stale docs.
note:
2026-09-19: outsideCode() in utils.ts splits the rendered HTML on ... and substitutes only between the pieces — a fence renders as 
, so one rule covers both. Code is literal, which is what writers expect. The other placeholders were never at risk: {{content}} is substituted last, so a page's text is inserted after they're consumed.

summary: No /health route for a platform healthcheck
detail: Railway (and any platform) wants a cheap endpoint that proves the process is up without depending on content. Today the shallowest check is / , which renders index.md through storage — on S3 that's a network round trip per probe, and a content mistake reads as a dead service.
note: 2026-09-20: /health in main.ts — a static Response, so the probe never touches storage.

summary: A pid file on a persistent volume can permanently block startup in a container
detail: claimPidFile() refuses to start when the pid file names a live process, checking only isAlive(). In a container the app is a low pid (often 1). After a hard restart (SIGKILL, OOM, platform recycle) the file survives on the volume naming pid 1, which is always alive — so the new process throws and the service never starts again: a crash loop with no bad input. stopServer() already has isDuckie() (ps, command line names main.ts); claimPidFile doesn't use it.
note: 2026-09-20: claimPidFile refuses only a live *duckdown* (heldByDuckie = isAlive && isDuckie, the check stopServer already used), and takes the guard as a parameter so both branches are tested deterministically. process.test.ts now runs two real servers for the refusal, and asserts a restart over a recycled pid.

summary: A deployment seeded from the example site ships a public admin/admin
detail: DUCKDOWN_SEED copies tests/example (or create's scaffold) when the content folder is empty, users.json included. That's right for local dev and wrong the moment the site is on the internet: the editor is at a known URL with known credentials. Needs a deliberate answer — an admin password from the environment at seed time, or a refusal to seed default credentials when DEBUG isn't set.
note: 2026-09-20: DUCKDOWN_ADMIN_PASSWORD (with DUCKDOWN_ADMIN_USER, default admin) is written into users.json at startup by ensureAdmin() — the secret lives in the platform, not in git, and changing it changes the password on the next restart. It rewrites only when the password actually changed, so a restart isn't an S3 PUT. Unset, nothing happens, which is every local run.

summary: GitHub reports 36 Dependabot alerts on master; duckdown has five dependencies
detail: The push to master printed 36 vulnerabilities (2 critical, 16 high). All 36 pointed at one manifest, client/package-lock.json — the Vue client, deleted on 2026-03-20 in the rewrite commit. None pointed at package.json or bun.lock, and none of the flagged packages (koa, axios, lodash, postcss, prismjs, minimist, loader-utils, node-forge…) is in the current tree, which is railroad, lucide-static and three dev dependencies. GitHub had not closed them when the manifest went.
note: 2026-09-21: checked against the alert API rather than guessed, then dismissed all 36 as not_used with the reason recorded on each. 0 open now. Left alone, a security page showing 36 alerts and 2 criticals teaches you to ignore it, and a real one in bun.lock would be lost in the noise.

summary: bun create leaves a half-scaffolded site: the postinstall hook doesn't run setup
detail: `bun create blueshed/duckdown x` prints `$ bun run create/setup.ts` and never runs it. Proved it's Bun 1.4.2, not the script: a bun-create.postinstall of `echo HELLO` prints its own command line and produces no output, and `sh -c 'echo > ran.txt'` writes no file anywhere. Bun does read the field — it strips it from the package.json it writes — it just doesn't execute it. The symptom is worse than first logged: without setup there is no .env, so DEBUG isn't set, so the server refuses to start over a missing COOKIE_SECRET — a message that says nothing about the real cause.
note: 2026-09-20: can't be fixed by changing the command, so duckdown stops depending on the hook. server/scaffold.ts spots a copy `bun create` left un-set-up (bun strips the bun-create key, so its absence plus a missing site/ and a present create/setup.ts is the signature) and the COOKIE_SECRET error carries the explanation and the one command that fixes it: bun run setup. Not auto-run: setup deletes tests/ and create/, and doing that silently because someone typed `bun dev` would be worse than the bug. Verified end to end on a faithful copy.

summary: DUCKDOWN_SEED fills a local folder but never a bucket, so an S3 deployment starts empty
detail: seedLocalSite() returns immediately when IS_S3 (`if (s3 || !seed || existsSync(target)) return`). With DUCKDOWN_BUCKET set, a fresh deployment therefore has no pages, no template and no users.json — the site 404s and nobody can sign in, with nothing in the logs to say why. There is no supported way to get a scaffolded site/ into a bucket; blueshed.co.uk needed a hand-written upload script (scripts/seed-bucket.ts there). The fix mirrors the local path: when the bucket has no pages/index.md, copy the seed folder up, then say so in the startup banner. Guard it the same way — seed only when the target is empty — so it can never overwrite a live site.
note: 2026-09-20: seedBucketSite() in storage.ts uploads DUCKDOWN_SEED when the bucket holds no pages/index.md, called from main.ts after seedLocalSite(). Guarded like the local path — only into an empty site, so it can never overwrite one being written — and it says in the log what it did, or that the seed folder wasn't there. Tested against the fake S3.

summary: A placeholder used twice in a template was only filled once
detail: The template was filled with .replace("{{title}}", fn), and String.replace with a string pattern replaces only the first occurrence. blueshed.co.uk's template used {{title}} in <title> and again in og:title, so every page published <meta property="og:title" content="{{title}}"> — the placeholder itself, on the live site.
note: 2026-09-20: fill() uses a global regex per placeholder, so a template may use one anywhere and as often as it likes; {{content}} is still filled last so a page's own text is never scanned. Found by checking the deployed page's meta tags.

summary: templates/ and static/ can't be edited, so a deployed site's template can only be changed out of band
detail: The editor reaches pages/ (and images through /edit/browse). templates/site.html, static/site.css and anything else under static/ are not editable. On a local site that's fine — edit the files. On a bucket-backed deployment the bucket is the only copy and is never re-seeded, so changing the template means writing to S3 by hand; blueshed.co.uk needed a script for it. Either let the editor open templates/ and static/ text files, or give duckdown a documented way to push them.
note: 2026-09-20: the editor has sections. fileRoutes(prefix, store, changed) in routes/files.ts is the file API over one folder; pages/, templates/ and static/ each get their own route rooted in their own folder, so none can reach across them and users.json (hashes, at the site root) is in none of them. The browser has pages | templates | static, and switching puts down whatever was open so a file can't be saved into the wrong folder. A template is neither markdown nor CSS, so the preview says so instead of rendering its placeholders as prose.

summary: Three URLs serve each page and each claims itself canonical
detail: Since folders are served by their index, /journey, /journey/ and /journey/index.html all answer 200. {{url}} reports whichever was asked for, so each is canonical for itself — duplicate content, three ways. The nav and wiki links both emit /index.html, which is the least tidy of the three. Pick one form: have the nav and wiki links emit the folder path, and have {{url}} normalise (drop a trailing index.html, keep one trailing-slash convention) so the other two point at it.
note: 2026-09-21: canonicalPath() in utils.ts is the one rule — index.md is /, a folder's index is /folder/, anything else is /page.html — and the canonical is computed from the key the request resolved to, not from the address asked for, so all three forms name the same page. The nav and markCurrent use the same rule, so the links crawlers follow are the canonical ones. The seed's template gained the canonical link (only the website's had it), the seed's own links were canonicalised, and the guide and reference say which of the three is the real address.

summary: layout: had no user anywhere, and the seed shipped a broken Tornado template
detail: Nothing in tests/example, .dev-site or blueshed.co.uk used layout:, so a feature with tests had never been used in practice. Worse, the seed shipped templates/site_tmpl.html — {{ handler.one_meta_value('title') }}, {% end %} — the Python duckdown's Tornado template. Nothing referenced it, it would render its own tags as text if anything did, and it appeared in the editor's template list looking like a real choice.
note: 2026-09-21: site_tmpl.html removed; templates/post.html added with a dated post in a new seed blog that uses it. {{date}} added so a template can show a page's date, sharing dateHtml() with the folder listings. Two test fixtures were quietly fighting over the name templates/post.html — the older layout test created and deleted it — which is why the new one failed only when the whole suite ran.

summary: dateHtml shows the previous day west of UTC
detail: new Date("2026-09-21") parses as UTC midnight but the Intl.DateTimeFormat formats in the server's local timezone: with TZ=America/New_York the seed post renders "20 September 2026" under datetime="2026-09-21", and the new server test (which expects 21 September) fails on such a machine. Passes on a UTC host, so deployment hides it. Pre-existing in the listings; moved into utils.ts unchanged. Fix: add timeZone: "UTC" to the formatter.
note: 2026-09-21: Intl.DateTimeFormat now takes timeZone: "UTC". A date: has no time in it, so it is a label, not a moment — it must read the same wherever the server runs. Proved by running the whole suite under TZ=America/New_York, and units.test.ts now asserts dateHtml directly.

summary: The plain-word guard is written twice, and template() is roundabout
detail: /^[\w-]+$/ guards both layout (line 39) and css (line 105): it is the path-traversal guard, so one plainName() helper keeps the two from diverging. template() could be names = plain(layout) ? [layout, "site"] : ["site"] instead of a loop with a continue. The inner name in renderPage's fill loop also shadows the outer name.

summary: The preview builds its own shell, so editing a template changes nothing in it
detail: A resource pane can now open templates/site.html beneath the page, but the preview never sees it: Preview.tsx wraps the rendered markdown in a shell of its own making, so a draft template body has nowhere to go and {{nav}} is missing from the preview entirely. /edit/mark/ should render the whole document through the real template, taking an optional draft template body in the request, and Preview should send the open resource's draft when it is the template the page uses.
note: 2026-09-21: server/page.ts holds parsePage() and pageHtml(); routes/site.ts and routes/mark.ts both go through it, so the preview is the real document — template, nav, {{pages}}, theme cascade. PUT /edit/mark/ takes JSON ({source, draft}) and answers {html, layout, meta}. An unsaved template is used when it is the one the page wears; a stylesheet still goes straight into the head with no round trip.

summary: Nothing says when the open template isn't the one the page uses

Say it once, in the pane, without blocking the edit — you may well be editing the template you are about to switch to.

summary: Static site export: pre-render the site to a static folder for CDN/static hosting
detail: Duckdown currently requires a running Bun server to render and serve pages. For static hosting (Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, S3 static hosting, Netlify) without an always-on process, duckdown could pre-render the site: walk pages/, render every non-draft page through pageHtml() to its canonical path (index.html, folder/index.html, page.html), and copy static/ and images/. Expose via a CLI command (e.g. bun run export [outDir]).
note: 2026-09-21: shipped in 0.1.0 as `bun run export` (server/export.ts). Writes every page at its one canonical address through pageHtml() — the same renderer the site route and the preview use — then copies static/. Drafts left out, {{edit}} empty, {{url}} from DUCKDOWN_ORIGIN. Reads through the storage layer, so it exports a folder or a live bucket. blueshed.co.uk runs on it.

summary: Client-side search: index published pages for readers to search the site
detail: As a site grows beyond a few folders, readers have no way to find content without clicking through the nav. Duckdown could generate a lightweight search index (e.g. /search.json holding titles, descriptions, headings, and clean text) rebuilt on page changes or export, paired with a small search modal or input template placeholder (e.g. {{search}}) that works without external services.
note: 2026-09-21: server/search.ts builds one entry per readable page (url, title, description, and plainText(body)); /search.json serves it, cached like the nav and dropped by routes/pages.ts on a write, and bun run export writes dist/search.json so it works published too. The matching is the site's own static/search.js — no dependency, no index format. Seed index is 12KB for 8 pages. Drafts excluded, and a test fetches every entry's url to prove no result 404s.

summary: The bin entries are never exercised
detail: 0.1.0 added bin: { duckdown, duckdown-export } so a site can depend on duckdown rather than vendor its server/. Nothing runs them: blueshed.co.uk calls node_modules/duckdown/server/main.ts by path, and no test installs the package. Either exercise them (a test that installs into a scratch folder and runs `bunx duckdown-export`) or drop them — config nothing reaches is the same as config that doesn't work.

detail: outPath("404.md") is "404.html", so a page at pages/404.md exports to dist/404.html, which is what static hosts serve for a miss — blueshed's serve.ts already looks for it. Nothing says so: not the README, not the skill, and the seed ships no 404.md, so nobody would discover it. Either document it and have the seed demonstrate it, or decide it isn't a feature and say what happens on a miss instead.
note: 2026-09-21: found while checking serve.ts's 404 branch was reachable — it is. | 2026-09-21: fixed: the seed ships pages/404.md; README, the skill's reference and the guide say what it does; served and exported (see n79).

summary: A content folder that goes missing serves 404s and says nothing
detail: seedLocalSite() runs once, at startup. Delete or move DUCKDOWN_PATH while the server is up and every page is a plain 404 with nothing in the log — /health still answers 200, so it looks like a routing or a port problem rather than an empty site. That contradicts the project's own rule that nothing fails silently. Either notice at request time that the configured root has gone and say so loudly (once, not per request), or reseed. Hit three times on 2026-09-21, by me, each time costing minutes of looking in the wrong place.
note: 2026-09-21: raised after the user hit it — "I could not navigate to blogs". | 2026-09-21: fixed: routes/site.ts noticeMissingRoot() says once, in the log, at the first miss after the folder goes (again if it goes a second time).

summary: The "Edit this page" button floats over the text on a narrow screen
detail: {{edit}} renders a position:fixed link at the bottom right. On a phone it sits over whatever is there — on /guide/pages.html it covers a row of the front-matter table. Only someone signed in sees it, so no reader is affected, but the author reading their own page is. Either dock it into the flow at the foot of the page below a certain width, or fade it until it is touched.
note: 2026-09-21: below 34rem .user-edit goes back into the flow at the foot of the page. Fixed with a sweep rather than on its own: 8 seed pages at 320/375/414/768 also turned up the front-matter table pushing the page sideways at 320, because a code span like templates/post.html is one unbreakable word that sets the column's minimum. overflow-wrap: anywhere on inline code (and on links, for bare URLs) fixes it; pre code is reset to normal because a fenced block scrolls.

summary: An export of nothing succeeds, so a misconfigured deploy publishes an empty site
detail: Reproduced: `DUCKDOWN_PATH=/nonexistent bun run server/export.ts out` prints '0 page(s) and 1 file(s)', exits 0, and leaves only search.json. On Railway the build then passes, serve.ts answers /health, and the deploy goes green with every page a 404. vashti is exposed to exactly this: its .railwayignore drops .env, railway.json sets no variables, so unless DUCKDOWN_PATH is set in the dashboard the exporter falls back to config.ts's default ./tests/example, which does not exist in a site that installs duckdown as a dependency. Fix: exportSite() throws (not process.exit - see Testing in CLAUDE.md) when it wrote zero pages, naming the storage root it read, and does so BEFORE rmSync(out) so a bad run never wipes a good dist. The import.meta.main caller lets it exit non-zero. Related to n68 (same silence, served side) - do them together. Also reconsider the ./tests/example default in config.ts: when that folder is absent and ./site exists, ./site is what both real sites mean. Tests: export.test.ts, an empty Storage and a missing folder both reject; the existing dist survives.
note: 2026-09-21: from a review of the two sites that depend on duckdown (Workshop/blueshed/website, Workshop/vashti). | 2026-09-21: fixed: exportSite renders first and throws before rmSync when there is nothing to publish, naming where it looked; main() returns the exit code. config.ts defaultSitePath() picks ./site when ./tests/example is absent. Existing dist survives (tested).

summary: serve.ts is copied byte-for-byte into both sites, untested, and miscounts page views
detail: website/serve.ts and vashti/serve.ts are identical (cmp) 60-line copies: the published flavour's server. It belongs in duckdown. Move it to server/serve.ts, export a `serveDist(dir, port)`/`route(req, dir)` that tests can call in-process (100% coverage applies), guard the Bun.serve behind import.meta.main, add bin `duckdown-serve`, and document `bun run node_modules/duckdown/server/serve.ts` as the published start command (README, skill's publishing section). This closes website ledger n3. Two defects to fix on the way in, both visible in the copy: (1) it calls logView() for every request except /health, so stylesheets, images and search.json are logged as 'view' lines and website's `bun run views` ranks /static/site.css among the most read - the served site logs pages only (routes/site.ts). Log only answers that are HTML (the found file ends .html, or the 404). (2) decodeURIComponent(url.pathname) throws URIError on a malformed escape such as /%E0%A4%A - answer 400, don't throw. Keep what is right about it: the traversal guard, the relative 301 for /blog -> /blog/ with the query kept, 404.html with status 404, max-age=300. Tests: traversal (/../x, encoded %2e%2e), folder redirect, query preserved, 404.html used when present and plain 404 when not, static not logged, malformed escape is 400. After release, each site deletes its serve.ts and points start at duckdown's.
note: 2026-09-21: from a review of the two sites that depend on duckdown (Workshop/blueshed/website, Workshop/vashti). | 2026-09-21: fixed: server/serve.ts, bin duckdown-serve, `bun run serve`; documented in README and the skill. Logs pages only; malformed escape is 400; tests/serve.test.ts. Published start command: `bun run node_modules/duckdown/server/serve.ts`. Follow-up in each site after release: delete its serve.ts and point start at that (closes website n3).

summary: A malformed percent-escape in a URL is a 500 with a stack in the log
detail: Reproduced in-process: handleSite(new Request('http://x/%E0%A4%A')) throws URIError: URI error, which routes/error.ts turns into a logged 500. Crawlers and scanners send these all day, so a served site's log fills with stacks that are nobody's bug. after() in utils.ts has the same decodeURIComponent and the same exposure on /static/*, /edit/pages/* etc. One helper in utils.ts (decode or null), used by both; a path that won't decode is a 400 'Bad Request' (and still a logged view on the site route). Tests in server.test.ts for / and /static/.
note: 2026-09-21: from a review of the two sites that depend on duckdown (Workshop/blueshed/website, Workshop/vashti). | 2026-09-21: fixed: utils.decodePath() and BadRequest; site route and serve.ts answer 400, after() throws BadRequest which handleError answers 400 without a stack.

summary: duckdown's base files are copied into each site and never upgrade
detail: CLAUDE.md calls static/site.css 'duckdown's base', but a site owns a copy made on the day it was scaffolded. summary: Two ways in, one scaffold: install (duckdown as a dependency, upgrades by tag) and create (own the code)

INSTALL (the documented default; what blueshed/website and vashti are): `bun add github:blueshed/duckdown#<tag>` then `bunx duckdown init`. Code stays in node_modules/duckdown/server/, scripts run it by that path, an upgrade is a tag bump. CREATE (ejecting: for someone who needs a different duckdown): `bun create blueshed/duckdown my-site`, as now. Code is ./server/, scripts run server/main.ts, and there is no upgrade path - bun create strips the history, so say plainly in the README that someone who wants ownership AND upstream merges should fork on GitHub instead. Build nothing for that. ONE SCAFFOLD: a single exported function (e.g. scaffold(root, { vendored: boolean }) in server/init.ts) writes everything the two share - site/ (index.md, theme.css, templates/site.html; NOT site.css or search.js, which come from server/base/ via n73's fallback), .env, .gitignore (node_modules, dist, .env, *.pid, .DS_Store, site/users.json), .claude/skills/duckdown, .claude/launch.json, a published-flavour Railway file with DUCKDOWN_PATH and DUCKDOWN_ORIGIN spelled out, a short CLAUDE.md, and package.json scripts dev/stop/export/start whose paths are the only thing the flag changes (start = duckdown's serve from n71). create/setup.ts calls it vendored after its tidy-up; a new bin `duckdown init` (import.meta.main guard, throws rather than process.exit) calls it in dependency mode, pinning the dependency to the installed package's own version tag. TESTS SURVIVE OWNERSHIP: setup() currently deletes tests/ and bunfig.toml, so the owner inherits 1,700 lines held at 100% coverage and loses the suite on day one - exactly when they intend to change the code. In create mode keep tests/, bunfig.toml and the seed they run against (tests/example); still remove feature.md, todo.jsonl, create/, and the railroad/bun-route skills only if the editor's tests don't need them (they don't; they are authoring aids - but keep them, an owner edits the editor). If keeping the suite proves impractical, stop and say why rather than quietly deleting it. MOVING BETWEEN THEM is possible and worth one README paragraph, not a command: to take ownership, copy node_modules/duckdown/server to ./server and repoint the scripts; to go back, delete ./server and add the dependency. The content never moves. ORDER: after n71 (serve) and n73 (server/base/), so the scaffold copies neither. summary: Search finds the page but not the place: index by section, and link to the heading
detail: Peter's report from vashti: searching a song title finds /jadd/ - a 559-line page of twenty songs - and drops the reader at the top. The belief was that the pages have no anchors. They do: renderMarkdown asks Bun.markdown for heading ids, so the exported page already has <h2 id="train-song">, duplicates numbered (same, same-1), and site.css already gives :target headings scroll-margin-top. What's missing is that the index has one entry per PAGE with all its text in one string, so a result can only ever link to the page. FIX, server side: one entry per SECTION. In buildIndex, render the page (renderMarkdown - do NOT reimplement Bun's slugger; read the ids out of the HTML so they can never disagree with the page) and split the rendered HTML at <h1-6 id=...>. Text before the first heading is the page's own entry (url = canonicalPath, as now). Each heading starts an entry { url: canonical + '#' + id, title: page title, section: heading text, description: '' , date, text: that section's words }. Get the words by stripping tags from the section's HTML and decoding the five entities, dropping <pre> blocks first as plainText does for fences; then plainText() and its tests either go or are reduced to what is still used - a line no test reaches is dead. Keep `description` on the page entry only. Index size stays about the same (same words, cut differently) - check vashti's search.json stays near its current 150KB. The sitemap (n77) must NOT take its URLs from this index any more if it does - it wants pages, not sections: give buildIndex's walk a page-level list both can use. FIX, browser side (static/search.js): score() gains the section heading between title and description (a word in the heading: 8). A result shows 'Page title - Section' and links to entry.url with its #id. Group so one page can't fill all eight slots: at most three sections per page, best first. extract() uses the section text. SECOND HALF - the words themselves, for a hit deep in a long section with no heading near it (vashti's news page: 950 lines, 27 headings, long entries): append a text fragment to the link - url + '#' + id + ':~:text=' + encodeURIComponent(the matched words as they appear in entry.text). The browser scrolls to and highlights the phrase; supported in Chrome, Safari 16.1+ and Firefox 131+, and a browser that doesn't know it ignores everything after ':~:' and still lands on the heading, so it degrades to the first half for free. Rules: use the first term's actual occurrence from entry.text (original case, not the lowercased copy), a few words of it (3-6) so it is unique enough, percent-encode, and '-' ',' '&' inside the text must be encoded too (encodeURIComponent leaves '-' alone: replace it with %2D, because a bare dash is fragment-directive syntax). For a page entry with no id the fragment is just '#:~:text=...'. A same-page result (you searched from the page the hit is on) must still scroll: setting location.hash to the same page is a fragment navigation, which works - test it by hand, and close the panel on click. This changes what search.json holds, so: the skill's reference.md search section, the guide page, CHANGELOG, and note for sites that forked search.js that an old search.js still works against the new index (extra `section` field ignored, urls now carry #ids - that is the point) - with n73's fallback most sites won't have a fork. Tests: search.test.ts - a page with two headings yields three entries with the right urls; duplicate headings get -1; a draft yields none; text in a fence is left out; heading text with & and an apostrophe. editor/happy-dom can load search.js against a staged index to assert grouping and the fragment encoding. Then check vashti by hand at 375: search 'train song', land on the song.

summary: On vashti a search result does not scroll: the text fragment cancels the jump to the heading
detail: Verified against a scratch copy of vashti exported with the unreleased tree and served by server/serve.ts, in the desktop app's browser at 375x812. Searching 'train song' gives the right results (Diamond Day - Train Song -> /jadd/#train-song:~:text=Train%20wheels%20beating%2C%20the%20wind, '-' encoded, panel inside the viewport, input 16px, no sideways scroll). A REAL CLICK on the first result loads /jadd/ and stays at the top: scrollY 0, the heading 3058px down. Isolated by navigating directly: '/jadd/#train-song' scrolls (scrollY 3042, heading 16px from the top); '/jadd/#train-song:~:text=...' does not; '/jadd/#:~:text=Train%20wheels%20beating' does not. So in this browser a text directive that isn't honoured also suppresses the element-id fallback. n82's detail said an unsupporting browser 'still lands on the heading' for free - that was my claim and it is wrong at least here (an embedded Chromium; document.fragmentDirective exists). It may well work in desktop Chrome and Safari; it must not depend on that. It passed on the seed presumably because the seed's pages are short or the check was same-page. FIX 1 - search.js owns the fallback. search.js is on every page, so on arrival: on 'load' (not DOMContentLoaded - vashti's /jadd/ has 22 images with no width/height, and the heading moves 3000px as they load), read location.hash (the browser strips the ':~:' part from it, so it is '#train-song'), find the element, and if the reader hasn't scrolled (scrollY === 0) and the element isn't already in view, el.scrollIntoView(). If the text fragment DID work the page is already scrolled and this does nothing. Keep the text fragment: where it works it is the better landing. Decode the id (decodeURIComponent, in a try that logs - no bare catch). FIX 2 - the panel has no height limit. With 8 results at 375 wide the panel is 1144px tall on an 812px screen (measured); it is position:absolute so the page grows and the input scrolls away from the results. In server/base/site.css: .search-results { max-height: min(60vh, 28rem); overflow-y: auto; overscroll-behavior: contain; } so the input stays put and the list scrolls. Check 320/375/768 and desktop. FIX 3 - body matches are substrings. 'train song' ranks /look/reviews.html#bbc and #all-music-guide 5th and 6th, because 'train' is inside 'constraints' and 'restraint', and the text fragment then points at 'constraints of domesticity'. score() already makes a title match start a word ('art' finds Articles, not Stuttgart); do the same for section, description and text - one word-start regex per term, built once per search, not per entry. The phrase for the text fragment should start at that same word-start hit. summary: The nav's order is the folders' alphabetical order and nothing can change it without renaming a URL
detail: buildNav lists folders by name. The reference says 'name folders so they sort', which means the URL carries the ordering (1-about/), and renaming an existing folder to reorder it breaks every link to it. On vashti alphabetical gives Heartleap, Diamond Day, Lookaftering, News, Some Things..., Wayward - the last album first, the sixties fourth, News in the middle; Peter wants the albums in the order they were made and News last, and /news/ can't move. Root stays first. Depth-first as now, so a folder's order applies among its siblings only. Non-integer values are ignored (treated as unset) and, per 'failures speak', logged once in development. Consider whether {{pages}} and {{sitemap}} should honour it too: {{pages}} is date-then-title for posts and should stay so; {{sitemap}} lists folders and should follow the nav's order so the two agree - do that. summary: The published server answers on any host; with DUCKDOWN_ORIGIN set, another host should 301 to it
detail: blueshed.co.uk and www.blueshed.co.uk will both point at the Railway service once the apex is on a CNAME-flattening DNS (website ledger n1), and the same for anotherday.co.uk. Today serve.ts serves the site on whichever host arrives, so a reader on the apex stays there; the canonical link says www, which keeps search engines straight but leaves two addresses in the wild. When DUCKDOWN_ORIGIN is set and the request's host (x-forwarded-host, then host) differs from the origin's host, answer 301 to origin + path + query - relative to nothing, this one must be absolute, that's the point. Skip when DUCKDOWN_ORIGIN is unset, for /health, and for localhost, so dev and healthchecks are untouched. Log the view as now. Tests: host match serves; mismatch 301s with the path and query kept; unset origin serves anything; /health never redirects. CHANGELOG line for sites: set DUCKDOWN_ORIGIN and the apex redirects to www for free.
note: 2026-09-22: raised while writing the apex runbook for both sites; a proxy-side redirect (Cloudflare rule) would do it but this keeps every record DNS-only. | 2026-09-22: built. serve.ts otherHost(): with an origin, x-forwarded-host, then Host, then the URL's host; a mismatch is 301 to origin + path + query; unset origin, the origin's own host, localhost and /health are served. serveDist takes origin as a fourth parameter (default empty), listen() passes DUCKDOWN_ORIGIN. Tested in serve.test.ts; 300 pass at 100%. CHANGELOG under Unreleased. A site picks it up by bumping its duckdown pin and having DUCKDOWN_ORIGIN set.

summary: Collections: pages/<folder>/collection.json gives each item an address, rendered through a template with prev/next
detail: Driving case: antonydonaldson.com (Workshop/tony-site), ~440 works in sections -> optional subsections -> items {src, title, caption, index, prints}. Data: an ordered array of groups, each with optional subgroups and items, next to the folder's index.md and read through storage (local or S3). Array order is the prev/next order; prev/next wrap; keyed by index or slug, never by name (1960 has two groups called London). Each item is a page at /<folder>/<slug>/ rendered through `layout: item` (templates/item.html) with {{item-src}}, {{item-thumb}}, {{item-title}}, {{item-caption}}, {{prev}}, {{next}}, {{group}} and {{groups}} (section and subsection nav, the current one marked). An item slug that collides with a page fails loudly (the export's checks, and the editor's Notice). Goes through pageHtml() so the site, the preview and the export all render it; parsePage() is where an item is looked up when no .md answers. The nav and search caches drop on a collection.json write (pagesChanged), which the pages route already does for anything under pages/. Skill (.claude/skills/duckdown) and the seed's guide pages describe it with the feature.
note: 2026-09-22: fixed. server/collection.ts: collection.json beside a folder's index.md, read through storage and cached like the nav (collectionsChanged(), called from routes/pages.ts beside pagesChanged and searchChanged). Each item is a page at /<folder>/<slug>/ through itemPage() + pageHtml(), so the site, the preview and the export render it identically. Decisions the item left open: the lookup is itemAt(pages, name), called from routes/site.ts when no .md answers, not inside parsePage() - parsePage is sync over a source string and an item lookup needs storage; the three folder addresses (/x, /x/, /x/index.html) all reach an item; an item's {{edit}} opens the collection.json it is written in. Slugs are [a-z0-9-] with accents folded, duplicates -1/-2 in file order, item-<n> for a title with nothing usable in it. A collision with a page is reported by collectionProblems() in the preview (Preview.tsx speaks it) and in bun run export, where --strict fails on it.

summary: Collection overviews: {{items}} is a thumbnail grid of the folder's collection, {{items by=<field>}} groups it by a field
detail: {{items}} on a collection folder's index page: the groups in order, each a grid of thumbnails linking to the item pages. {{items by=index}}: one grid per distinct value of that field, in order of first appearance (or sorted when the values are years); an item whose field is the string "skip" is left out. The year fallback tony-site needs (index, else a 4-digit year found in the title or caption) is a documented option on the placeholder, `{{items by=index year}}` or similar, not a rule baked into the field. Generated HTML with plain classes (.collection, .group, .item, .thumb), styled by theme.css through the variables; no loops in templates, exactly like {{pages}} and {{nav}}.
note: 2026-09-22: fixed. {{items}}, {{items <collection>}}, {{items by=<field>}} and {{groups}} (also with a name), filled by fillCollections() over the page body outside <code> and again over the template, before {{content}}. Generated HTML with .collection/.group/.items/.item/.thumb, styled from --thumb and --thumb-gap in server/base/site.css. Per the porting session: the year fallback is dropped (the converter writes an explicit index on every item); a heading's id is the field's value when it can be a fragment and a slug when it can't (fragmentId), so a template can write href="/works/#{{item-index}}"; "labels": {"<field>": {"<value>": "<label>"}} makes the heading "1967 - California"; "skip" leaves an item out and also fills {{item-<field>}} as nothing, so that href lands at the top of the overview rather than at #skip.

summary: A collection's images may live at a root outside static/: an "images" setting in collection.json
detail: tony-site's originals, 128px thumbnails (<name>_tn.png) and banners are on S3 at ad.blueshed.info/images/{original,thumbnails,banners}. collection.json takes an optional "images" base URL; {{item-src}} and {{item-thumb}} are built from it and the item's src, and without it they resolve under the site's own static/images/. The thumbnail naming rule (a suffix) is a setting too, defaulting to _tn.
note: 2026-09-22: fixed. "images" is a base URL, or {src, thumb, suffix, extension} - thumb for a separate thumbnails folder and extension for thumbnails that are all .png whatever the original is, which is what ad.blueshed.info needs. suffix defaults to _tn and goes before the extension. Without the setting both resolve under /static/images/. An item with no src has no src and no thumb rather than a link to a folder.

summary: Items are pages to search, the sitemap and the export
detail: buildSite() walks pages/; a collection's items must be in the same walk so search.json carries an entry per item (title, caption as the body), the sitemap lists their addresses, and `bun run export` writes each item at /<folder>/<slug>/index.html. brokenLinks() checks the thumbnails' targets. One walk, one cache, as now.
note: 2026-09-22: fixed. buildSite() loads a collection.json it meets in its own walk and emits one Entry (title, the caption as the words) and one PageRef per item, so /search.json, dist/search.json and sitemap.xml carry them. export.ts renders each item at <folder>/<slug>/index.html through the same pageHtml. brokenLinks() checks the thumbnails for free, since they are ordinary src attributes - an absolute images base is skipped like any off-site link. The same walk now also returns the aliases (n93), so it is still one walk and one cache.

summary: Old addresses survive a move: a page or item can carry aliases that 301 to it
detail: tony-site's ~440 works are at flat URLs /<slug> today and those must keep working after the port. Rather than an option to mount a collection's items at the site root (which makes every miss a lookup across every collection and lets items shadow pages), items live at /<folder>/<slug>/ and a page or item lists `aliases:` (front matter for a page, a field for an item, or a generated list in collection.json); a request for an alias is a 301 to the canonical address. The export writes each alias as a tiny HTML redirect page (meta refresh + canonical) so the published flavour keeps them too. A parity check that follows redirects sees the same page.
note: 2026-09-22: fixed, as aliases rather than a root mount (the porting session confirmed nothing needs the flat URLs to answer 200). "aliases" is a field on an item and repeatable front matter on a page (added to KEYS in markdown.ts); buildSite() collects both and aliasTarget() matches on the decoded path, so /l%22etoile-1976 finds the alias l"etoile-1976. The site answers 301 to the canonical address; the export writes a small redirect page (canonical + meta refresh) at <alias>/index.html under the decoded name, which serve.ts finds after its own decodePath, so a published copy keeps them. An alias that is already a page leaves the page alone and is reported. Known limit, opened as n95: a filesystem or host that can't hold a name with a quote or a backtick in it can't keep that alias in the published flavour.

summary: Editor: a collection pane — edit titles and captions inline, reorder, add an item by dropping an image, swap an image in place, manage groups
detail: Last and lowest priority; the site can go live with collection.json edited as a file. Add an item: upload the original through the browse route and write a 128px thumbnail with Bun.Image (present in Bun 1.4.2). Swap an image: same filename, cache-bust with ?v=<mtime or hash>. Add, rename, remove groups. Reference: tony-site src/edit (delta + railroad) and src/lib/s3.ts. No undo in duckdown: rely on bucket versioning on S3, and say so in the skill.

summary: A published alias whose old address holds a character a filesystem won't take is dropped without a word
detail: An alias is exported as <alias>/index.html under the name a request decodes to, so serve.ts and any host that maps a path to a file find it - including l"etoile-1976 and don’t-write-everything-down on macOS and Linux (tests/serve.test.ts proves the round trip). A filesystem that won't take the character (Windows refuses ") or a host that normalises names silently loses that alias, and the export says nothing. Either check that each alias name round-trips and say so when it doesn't, or write a _redirects map beside dist/ for hosts that read one. The served flavour answers 301 from the index and needs none of this, so it only bites a site that publishes.

summary: {{items by=<field>}} can order its groups by value: sort=asc or sort=desc
detail: Groups come in first-appearance order, which for a collection written newest first is newest first; the old antonydonaldson.com shows oldest first, the one parity difference left. sort=asc|desc orders the groups by value, numbers as numbers (years) and the rest by string; items inside a group keep the file's order.
